To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of academic records to predict students' dropouts in higher education is a promising strategy.

(i) the best classification model for predicting students' dropout is a logistic regression model that does not take into account the course to which students are committed; (ii) the best classification models for predicting students' drop out have an accuracy between 0.70 and 0.75; (iii) the most important features for predicting students' dropping out are related to the number of subjects failed and the average grade;
1) the use of academic records for predicting student drop out is promising and 2) considering the target course as a relevant feature for predicting student dropouts is not a good idea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the factors behind students' dropout and with developing predictive models that can be used for early detection of at-risk students in higher education
identifying and characterizing students with high probability to drop out, as well in the early stages of their studies as later in the academic career.

the development and evaluation of a predictive model to support early detection of student dropout, and to understand the causes that lead students to dropout, in order to support the development of more effective actions to prevent it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
considering the course in the model does not lead to better performance than not considering it.
the course to which a target student is formally enrolled is not a relevant feature to predict dropout.
the proposed approach is able to detect dropout with a high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, given a student's academic record, it is possible to detect students with high probability to drop out.
the course is not a good predictor of the dropout.
the course in which the target student has been committed is not a relevant feature for predicting the dropout.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the particular case studied in this paper, it is possible to detect students with high probability to drop out with high accuracy using only the academic records.

the academic records are a valuable resource that can be exploited for predicting student drop out, and that the employed classification model can be used as a decision support tool to help higher education institutions to better understand the underlying factors behind the drop out problem.
the academic records are indeed a rich source of features that can be exploited for predicting students who are more likely to drop out.
